extra: The first stage load reaches this window. Code, map data and any padding still need their exact boundaries.
Second stage payload loaded at $C800. Individual asset boundaries remain to be classified.

comments.text: Advance the active slot's actor type, choose a facing frame by comparing its X coordinate with Arthur and initialize its frame delay. Shift it four pixels up and occasionally select type $13.
On a nonzero scroll phase, advance the current sprite frame. Reaching frame $37 moves the actor down four pixels and switches it to actor type four.
Every eighth value of $BC advance the shape by two. At shape $0E or later, clear the flags and advance the actor type before the common positioning path.
On scroll phase three, move the shape backward by two. Below shape four, deactivate the slot and its linked slot if present, then decrement the optional actor count.
Age the frame delay or jump to the transition for a screen-edge position. Depending on pose flags, move down then sample terrain through $3D15 and $3C29.

Use the immediate counter to number the actor. A negative count retires it. Otherwise decrement the counter, save its old value in the slot and advance the type before setting the hit count, random countdown and shape $C3.
Initialization consumes this immediate value and decrements it for the next actor. The value becomes the slot's tile-pointer index.
Age the delay. On expiry at shape $C3, advance the shape and spawn type $57 with shape $C5 and coordinate offsets. Check hits and replace two tiles if the slot changes type.
Three low bytes indexed by the actor's initialization value when it changes type.
Three high bytes paired with $895F. The target receives tiles $60 and $61 one row apart.
Select shape $C5 through $C8 from the phase and enter the resident shape setter.
Advance type, clear the state, set the hit counter to three and choose a random initial delay.
Choose shape and facing using the side of Arthur. When the timer expires, toggle the attack bit unless the proximity test blocks it. Entering the attack phase spawns a type $5A projectile.
Set a short delay and choose a Y step from the distance to Arthur. Select X step by facing. Spawn the projectile and offset its Y by four.
Signed unit steps for the two facing values passed to the linked actor allocator.
Pass shape $D2 to the resident shape setter.
Zero the actor's X and clear the resident scroll gate. Set the gate to $0C at fine positions $24–$26, and retire the slot from $27 onward.
Use the scroll patch condition, section, coarse position and Arthur's height to choose the resident scroll mask. At coarse X $46 or beyond clear the mask and retire the actor.

Initialize shape $D4 and a run index. Move along the terrain run, carrying Arthur vertically when his position passes the bounds test. At a masked counter match remove the next $A1 tile, update the row and chunk cursors and change type when the run ends.
The initial run index for a new type $5C slot. The initialization increments it after assigning it.
Patched to INY or NOP depending on the run index before evaluating Arthur's position.
Set to seven or fifteen for the two groups of run indexes.
Target phase two or twelve, paired with the mask at $8B18.
Apply the resident coordinate helper. On phase zero under mask $0F, age the shape up to $D6.
Give the slot a serial index from the operand and increment the operand for the next slot. The first slot sets the IRQ operand to five. Advance type, set eight hits and choose a random countdown.
The immediate index copied to the new slot's $19B4 field. The type $60 update reads the same byte to decide when to set the scroll gate.

Set the scroll gate once the initialization count reaches four. Alternate shapes $DA and $DB. On expiry use a random gate and the optional actor limit to spawn type $61. Check hits and decrement the remaining count if this slot changes type.
Decremented at $8C22 when a type $60 slot changes type. Zero enters the stage completion path.
Five countdowns indexed by the parent slot's assigned index and copied to its new type $61 slot.
Move up two pixels while the rise countdown is active. When it expires, choose shape and direction from Arthur's X. Later updates follow terrain and run the hit check.
Two signed directions selected by the comparison with Arthur at the end of the rise.

Sample the terrain. If the slot is still on its sideways path, step left or right before testing the four cached contact properties. When they are all zero, enter the falling state and add four to Y on the same update.
Take a free entry among four descriptor owners or retire if all are occupied. Save the owner index, choose shape $DE–$E1 and initialize motion and hit state before advancing the type.
Resolve the live descriptor using the owner index. Use the mode flag to animate the lead piece and launch type $65, or adjust the projection that positions the trailing pieces.
Advance the signed angle toward Arthur on suitable phases, then update the lead piece's facing. A random result can set the mode for launching a detached piece.
Project horizontal and vertical offsets for three pieces, writing the coordinates back into the active sprite descriptor.
Add the descriptor's first offset pair to the actor position and compare it with Arthur using fixed and shape-based extents. Mark the contact properties when the test passes.
Test at the lead piece position and restore the original slot coordinates afterward. A hit from a qualifying weapon type decrements the hit and weapon counts and clears the weapon slot.
Select one of four shapes using the phase, then enter the resident shape setter.
Four shape codes for the detached piece, selected at $8E6F.
Twenty-four mode bytes indexed by actor slot. The type $63 initializer clears the byte for its slot.
Four actor slot indexes, initialized to $FF by $9123. A new type $63 claims a negative entry.
Four descriptor pointer low bytes selected by the owner index.
Four high bytes paired with the table at $8E95.
Four fourteen-byte composite descriptors. A count and colour precede four sprite pointers with X and Y offsets, which the actor updates during motion.

At columns $6D through $70, clear bit 1 in the sixteen bytes beginning at $293D. Select a value for $1C83 based on column $74. When $CB reaches seven, advance the stage section and reinitialize scrolling.
When the vertical region reaches $2E, clear active slots whose collision classes are outside zero and three. Set the stage flag at $4728 according to the coarse and fine vertical scroll.
If the stage flag is set and Arthur's X coordinate is below $20, replace the flag value with $0C.

Copy eight run descriptors into the working arrays. Resolve each descriptor's chunk pointer and add its column offset and row displacement. Write tile $A1 down each column and advance to the chunk below after row nine.
Use the current chunk selector and row in $05 and $03. Add the per-run column displacement, then use the row table at $1BD6 for the vertical displacement.
Advance the row, and at row ten reset it to zero and add four to the pointer selector. Repeat until the run counter reaches zero.
Eight starting column offsets added to the chunk pointer.
Eight row indexes copied to $8FD4 and also used as each run's initial row.
Eight starting chunk selectors copied to $8FDC.
Eight run lengths copied to $8FE4.
Eight working row bytes initialized from the descriptor table at $8FBC.
Eight working chunk selectors initialized from $8FC4.
Eight working lengths initialized from $8FCC.

Section 06 has 32 ordered spawn records. Each six-byte record contains a 16-bit X tile, a 16-bit Y tile, packed sub-tile offsets and the actor ID. The scan at $30B3 advances after allocating the actor.

Section 07 has 21 ordered spawn records. Each six-byte record contains a 16-bit X tile, a 16-bit Y tile, packed sub-tile offsets and the actor ID. The scan at $30B3 advances after allocating the actor.
Section 06 has 16 optional spawn positions. Each record holds the two tile coordinates and one packed sub-tile byte. The bounded search at $3175 tests visibility and a random condition.
Section 07 has 0 optional spawn positions. Each record holds the two tile coordinates and one packed sub-tile byte. The bounded search at $3175 tests visibility and a random condition.
Set $CA to four, run the terrain edit script at $915D and draw eight vertical tile runs. Patch overlay and resident operands for the section.
Set the four trigger values at $8E91 to $FF. Then tail-call the terrain patch reader at $2FCD on the second script at $9134.
A terminated sequence consumed by $2FCD at the end of the stage setup. Each record selects a chunk, column, row, count minus one and the tile bytes to write.
Script passed to $2FCD before the vertical runs. It uses the same chunk and position byte layout as $9134 and ends in $FF.
Three little-endian start addresses for stage 4 music. The resident stage setter copies the six bytes into index six of the SID song table.
Stage 4 supplies this starting address for voice 1 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Stage 4 supplies this starting address for voice 2 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Stage 4 supplies this starting address for voice 3 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Three note and control phrases ending with return command $8B. The track-six walk from the three start pointers did not reach these entry points.
The current packed stage payload includes a byte-for-byte copy of stage 3 music data through $98A2. The three active pointers refer to their own earlier sequence region.
Copied stage 2 stream suffix through $9A51. This copy is reproduced by the disk decoder for this stage.
Copied stage 1 stream suffix through $9D01. This copy is reproduced by the disk decoder for this stage.
Zero-filled end of the loaded stage music window through $9FFF. Terrain chunk entries start after the $A000 page boundary.
Loaded 32-byte prefix before the first 200-byte terrain chunk. The entry snapshots share byte $55 followed by zeros. Layout pointers start at $A020.

Use the tile code as the index into the $B6 page selected by $2EEF. $48CC subtracts the selected byte from the player's ground-aligned Y value.
Surface offsets for the other terrain bank. $2EEF loads $B7 as the page for the pointer at $C4/$C5.
Tile properties for the first terrain bank. $3C29 maps nearby character-screen positions through this table and stores the attribute bytes at $EE-$F5.
Second terrain bank's tile attributes. $2EEF selects page $B9 for the pointer at $C2/$C3.
Colour lookup by terrain character code. The first bank case in $2EEF selects this page for $4BF8.
Colour lookup by terrain character code. The second bank case in $2EEF patches $4BF8 to this page.
Top-left character codes indexed by the tile number. $5010 and $5027 read this page.
Top-right character codes paired with the left half by $4FF6. $5016 and $5031 read this page.
Bottom-left character codes for the lower half of each tile. $5057 and $506E read this page.
Bottom-right character codes for the lower half of each tile. $505D and $5078 read this page.
Continuation of the bottom-right tile-to-character page at $BF00, starting at tile $BE. The page runs through tile $FF.
Eleven 64-byte VIC sprite slots starting at pointer $20. These slots match in all five stage images and render projectile silhouettes and small circular effects.

Stage sprite slots at pointers $2B through $97. Includes rounded enemy poses, circular objects and the curved pieces of larger creatures. The 64th byte of each slot is outside the 24 by 21 pixel raster.
Start of sprite 3B in stage 4. The VIC reads 21 rows of three bytes per slot and advances the base by 64 bytes.
